Recipe uses 6,102 of the 6,162 table rows (15.34 h): 33 rows of one movie whose table times are in the wrong unit, 3 rows without an audio segment and 24 rows of the same segment with different emotions are dropped; 6 same-segment same-emotion rows are kept by default (exclude_duplicates). Clips over 30 s are removed in all splits, including test (maintainer, 2026-10-28). Rights in the films are unaddressed (needs-confirmation list).

Implemented with 7 classes (angry / disgust / fear / happy / neutral / sad / surprise); uses all 420 clips. A perceptually validated corpus: every clip was rated three times in a blind listening test (73% recognition, kappa 0.59) and all judgements are released; the recipe uses the intended emotion only.
Only the paper's bibliographic data and abstract were checked; whether and how it is distributed was not checked.

The type of procedure comes from the spreadsheet Notes (EULA); not checked individually. Made a candidate on 2026-10-14 under the revised policy (maintainer's decision: manual access steps, label types and automatic labels are not reasons to exclude).

Recipe exists (egs3/anad/cls): 566 clips after 768 near-identical clips were removed (two groups of 386 and 382 that appear under different videos and labels; confirmed by listening). Every remaining clip also contains the same female voice ("ava smi...") with slightly different background sound; the cause is unknown. Labels are per video and their correspondence to chunks is unverified; almost all clips come from two videos (V7 angry, V8 happy).

Second look 2026-10-28: the Zenodo record (CC BY 4.0, open) only archives the 2016 Asian Journal of Science and Technology paper PDF about a five-emotion Arabic corpus; it contains no audio, so it is not a data source.

Implemented with 5 classes (angry / fear / happy / neutral / sad); by default 2,421 of the 2,474 clips are used (53 duplicate recordings are left out by exclude_duplicates; false uses all). The license is not stated and the authors are to be asked (not yet contacted). Only recordings accepted by at least five of eight judges are in the release. 75% of the clips are sentences whose emotion is fixed, so the words give the label for them.

Implemented with 7 classes (angry / disgust / fear / happy / neutral / sad / surprise); uses 3,211 clips by default. Left out: other emotions (314), 16 clips of the same sound with different emotions, and 14 same-emotion duplicates (exclude_duplicates). The 25 babies' voice clips (Bonus) are used (exclude_bonus can drop them). The rights of the original movie / TV / YouTube material are not documented and are awaiting the project members' judgement.

Labels are social attitudes (friendly, distant, dominant, seductive), not emotion categories. Made a candidate on 2026-10-14 under the revised policy (maintainer's decision: manual access steps, label types and automatic labels are not reasons to exclude).

Recipe exists (egs3/audiospeechsentiment/cls, TRAIN only, 250 clips). Labels are sentiment (positive / negative / neutral), not categorical emotions, and match the polarity of the meaning of the sentence read (all recordings of the same sentence have the same label, so the sentiment lives in the words). The 110 TEST clips have no labels.

Audio-video from video conferences simulating remote work. Access is requested with an institutional e-mail account on the Queen's University Dataverse (approval in 5-7 days). Added at the request of the literature database (2026-10-23).

Implemented with 8 classes; uses 3,218 of 3,220 clips (a byte-identical pair with different labels is always dropped). Labels are the perceived emotion judged by three annotators watching the videos; no agreement figure. The rights in the YouTube material are unaddressed (needs-confirmation list).

Implemented with 5 classes (angry / happy / neutral / sad / surprise, no disgust or fear); by default 1,459 of 1,467 clips are used (8 same-sound groups lose one file each; exclude_duplicates false uses all). Fifteen validators recognised the intended emotion 80.5% of the time. The intensity field is determined by the emotion, so it is not an independent label.

Implemented with 6 classes (angry / disgust / fear / happy / sad / surprise); uses all 792 clips. A panel of 10 validators recognised the target emotion 76.05% of the time. Mendeley version 1 has the audio; version 2 does not.

Not used: no voice difference between emotions could be heard, and emotions appear to be separated by sentence content (maintainer's listening 2026-10-23, confirmed with 100 Whisper transcripts). Officially 5 speakers, but listening and a speaker model suggest one person. Both checks were provisional and of low reliability.
Implemented with 5 classes (angry / fear / happy / neutral / sad). Uses 692 clips after removing 58 duplicates of the same sound (confirmed by the maintainer's listening).

Hugging Face access is manual (owner approval required) and the card body cannot be read before approval. License: other. Made a candidate on 2026-10-14 under the revised policy (maintainer's decision: manual access steps, label types and automatic labels are not reasons to exclude).

Second look 2026-10-28: BAUM-1 (UCI): 1,184 video clips from 31 subjects with spontaneous facial expressions and speech in 13 emotional and mental states (happiness, anger, sadness, disgust, fear, surprise, boredom, contempt, confusion, neutral, thinking, concentrating, bothered); face-oriented video database; download by e-mail to the authors.

Second look 2026-10-28: a face-centred audio-visual database of 1,047 video clips of 286 subjects, extracted from movies and TV programmes in several languages; BAUM-2 is built for facial expression recognition, so the labels are expected to be video-based; the emotion scheme was not verified here. UCI page CC BY 4.0; download by e-mail request to the authors.

Second look 2026-10-28: 1,935 recordings of 7 Arabic words by 61 speakers (45 male, 16 female) at three levels of expressed emotion (0 low, 1 neutral, 2 high positive or negative emotion); the label is an intensity level, not an emotion category (README). No license statement.

First review 2026-10-28: motion-capture gesture corpus: 76 h, 30 speakers, 8 emotions (neutral, happiness, anger, sadness, contempt, surprise, fear, disgust), English 60 h, Chinese 16 h, Spanish 2 h, Japanese 2 h; emotion labels are frame-level and per recording session. The speech is not segmented into labelled utterances; Hugging Face BEAT2 is Apache-2.0 per the DB. How to cut utterance-level labels is undecided.

Commercial data from BedVibe Studio. GitHub only introduces it. Moved to needs_decision on 2026-10-14 under the revised policy (maintainer's decision: manual access steps, label types and automatic labels are not reasons to exclude).

Second look 2026-10-28: Belfast natural database: clips of 10-60 s from 100 speakers (recorded discussions and TV programme extracts) with FEELTRACE continuous interpretation files; the labels are continuous traces, not categories. Distribution was not confirmed.

Implemented with 7 classes (angry / disgust / fear / happy / neutral / sad / surprise). Uses 4,460 clips after removing 63: byte-identical duplicates, groups with conflicting metadata, and clips containing several takes (maintainer's decision, 2026-10-23).

First review 2026-10-28: BIIC-NNIME: dyadic Mandarin acted conversations by 43 actors, 5,596 clips (5,028 in the DB's count). Free for academic and non-profit research: sign the EULA and send it with proof of affiliation (students need their supervisor's signature).

First review 2026-10-28: Mandarin podcast speech, 70,000 utterances (147 h), at least 5 annotators per utterance with primary and secondary emotions (MSP-PODCAST protocol). Academic license free (the institution signs an agreement); the audio comes from CC-BY / CC-BY-SA podcasts; commercial licensing available for a fee. Categorical emotion options per the MSP-Podcast scheme.

Implemented with 7 classes (angry / disgust / fear / happy / neutral / sad / surprise); uses all 936 clips of the 48 kHz version (the 192 kHz version holds the same recordings); both intensities are used. Non-commercial license. No listening test was found in the sources read.

Speaking-style captions added to existing speech corpora (over 10 million automatic, about 0.36 M human), plus three newly recorded datasets. Added at the request of the literature database (2026-10-23).

10,000 pairs recorded for CapSpeech by one voice actor performing fine-grained emotional variations. The audio is gated on Hugging Face (value: auto). Added at the request of the literature database (2026-10-23).

[WARNING] The recipe's data source (a Hugging Face mirror) is an unofficial redistribution of a corpus licensed for a fee and should not be used. The distributor ChineseLDC (CLDC-SPC-2005-010) licenses it for a fee (archived page of 2020-05-01: from CNY 5,000 domestic non-commercial to CNY 105,000 foreign commercial). The widely used 1,200-clip version (EmoBox etc.) is a re-upload by an individual to Baidu AI Studio on 2023-04-16, and the Hugging Face mirror was confirmed to hold the same files (size and modification time match for 20 files). No source allows free redistribution. Tao et al. 2008, which SER papers cite for it, describes a single-speaker speech-synthesis corpus and does not mention emotion. No paper by the creators was found. The recipe is kept with a warning by the maintainer's decision (2026-10-23). Details: reports/2026-10-23_casia_db_update.md.

Second look 2026-10-28: Cantonese Audio-Visual Emotional Speech (CAVES): 10 speakers x 50 sentences x 7 emotions = 3,500 recordings (full-HD video), validated by 15 native perceivers; the paper (CC BY) says the dataset is freely available for research purposes through an online form.

Implemented with 6 classes (angry / disgust / fear / happy / neutral / sad), Telugu and English. Uses 4,164 of the 4,204 released clips; 40 are removed: 10 misplaced copies, 1 " - Copy", 2 with the same sound under different labels, and 27 second-or-later copies of the same sound under the same label (the last 27 by the maintainer's decision, 2026-10-23).

The only source is a 2000 PhD thesis; its text could not be obtained and no distributor was found. Values from Table I of the MSP-Podcast paper (its Avail column shows ✗, but the paper does not define the column).

Second look 2026-10-28: Chinese multimodal sentiment dataset of 2,281 video segments in the wild with fine-grained unimodal and multimodal annotations; the labels are sentiment scores/polarity, not emotion categories (THUIAR page).

Second look 2026-10-28: CH-SIMS v2.0: 4,402 supervised and 10,161 unsupervised instances; classification labels are five sentiment classes (negative, weakly negative, neutral, weakly positive, positive) and regression labels from -1 to 1, not emotion categories (THUIAR page).

A small crowd-sourced annotation set of emotion and speaking style for 500 clips (100 Common Voice, 400 VoxCeleb). The Hugging Face release is a single parquet file (modality: text only) without audio. Excluded because there is no audio (not because of size).
No raw audio or video is distributed; only non-invertible features are public. Labels require an EULA (paper, Privacy and Ethics).

The official SDK distributes only anonymised features (its README says raw videos cannot be shared). The hosts said to serve raw data were unreachable on 2026-10-12. Of the 3,227 IDs in the SDK's standard split file cmu_mosei_std_folds.py, 2,768 are YouTube-style (11 characters) and 459 are numeric only; what the numeric IDs refer to is unverified. Second look 2026-10-28: the official acoustic data are COVAREP features; no official raw-WAV release was found. Web search results point to community WAV copies on Hugging Face whose owners warn about copyright and YouTube terms (not checked). Re-extracting audio from the YouTube videos is the only route to full 23,453 segments.
The official SDK distributes only anonymised features, and its FAQ says raw videos cannot be shared. Labels are sentiment polarity, not emotion categories.
Only the paper's bibliographic data and abstract were checked; whether and how it is distributed was not checked.
The Hugging Face files are only csv and json, no audio (modality: text). Card: "Created using codaco.app".

Labels are three classes, neutral / non-neutral female / non-neutral male, not emotion categories (non-neutral is judged by paralinguistic events such as laughter and crying). Made a candidate on 2026-10-14 under the revised policy (maintainer's decision: manual access steps, label types and automatic labels are not reasons to exclude).
Only text and audio/visual features are released because of copyright, privacy and video-site terms (paper abstract).

Implemented with 6 classes (angry / disgust / fear / happy / neutral / sad); uses all 7,442 clips. The label is the intended emotion; the crowd ratings are distributed but not used (audio-only majority agrees with the intention for only 42-48% of clips). Five groups of identical sound are kept (four with different emotions); sentences are shared with SES-ED.
The paper does not describe distribution, and a search on 2026-10-13 found no distributor. The corpus has no name of its own.

Implemented with 7 classes. Uses all 4,160 clips (the 15 train clips over 30 s are dropped by remove_long_short). The repository's NOTICE says it incorporates ESD (research use only), but no overlap with ESD's audio or sentences was found, so that condition is not applied and the data is treated as Apache-2.0 (open) per the card (maintainer's decision, 2026-10-23).

For supporting the diagnosis of psychological distress such as depression and PTSD; labels are not emotion categories. Access by submitting a signed application, limited to academic and non-profit researchers. Made a candidate on 2026-10-14 under the revised policy (maintainer's decision: manual access steps, label types and automatic labels are not reasons to exclude).

[VALUABLE AS CONVERSATIONAL SPEECH] Keeps 2,541 two-person dialogues intact, with utterance order, topic, dialogue act and transcript (21.7 h). The current recipe does utterance-level SER without the dialogue structure, but the data may be needed for future dialogue research (dialogue-level emotion recognition, context-aware SER, conversational speech) (maintainer's assessment, 2026-10-24). Labels are DailyDialog's annotations of the text, which the voice actors followed; they were not assigned by listening to the audio. The recipe uses 23,772 utterances, leaving out the valid-side copy of one shared recording.

Labels are vocal polarity (negative / neutral / positive), not emotion categories. The public part is about 1% of the whole (about 3 hours, about 2,000 utterances): one speaker pair, one distance, iPhone X only. Small size is not a reason to exclude. Made a candidate on 2026-10-14 under the revised policy (maintainer's decision: manual access steps, label types and automatic labels are not reasons to exclude).

Labels are types of non-verbal sounds (16 kinds: cough, yawn, laughter, crying, scream, ...), not emotions. The public part is about 1% of the whole. Made a candidate on 2026-10-14 under the revised policy (maintainer's decision: manual access steps, label types and automatic labels are not reasons to exclude).

First review 2026-10-28: induced (not acted) Italian emotional speech: 9,697 samples from 68 speakers in 7 states (anger, sadness, happiness, fear, surprise, disgust, guilt, plus neutral samples); a 1,564-sample prototypical subset was selected by self- and external assessment. Restricted on Zenodo: send an EULA signed by a permanent university staff member (non-commercial academic).

Second look 2026-10-28: Danish Emotional Speech database: four actors, five emotions, about 30 minutes (DB count 419 utterances); a 20-listener test gave 67.3% recognition. Where and how it is distributed was not found in the sources read (the 1997 paper only).

First review 2026-10-28: dynamic facial expression database: 16,372 clips obtained from the Internet (DB count) with expression labels; the labels were assigned from the video (facial expressions), not from the voice. Non-commercial research only; e-mail from a university account to receive a password.

Directly downloadable from Zenodo (177 MB). The archive contains mu-law audio files (.ul) and dialogue-act annotations (downloaded and listed). Made a candidate under the policy of 2026-10-14 (intents and dialogue acts are not emotions, but are future training targets for models of paralinguistic information).

Implemented with 4 classes (angry / happy / neutral / sad) from the crowd part: 160,357 of the 160,366 official-list clips; the 9 clips of 4 same-sound groups with different emotions are always dropped. Labels are perceived (Dawid-Skene aggregate of crowd listeners); the speakers were non-professional actors. Open license (LicenseRef-golos-public).
Only the paper's bibliographic data and abstract were checked; whether and how it is distributed was not checked.

First review 2026-10-28: EARS: 107 speakers, 100 h of clean 48 kHz speech; the emotional part has 22 emotions (including nuanced ones such as serenity and adoration) per speaker with three sentences and a free description each. License CC BY-NC 4.0 (README). The size of the emotion part was not stated in the sources read.

Implemented with 4 classes (angry / happy / neutral / sad); uses all 1,164 clips. Labels are what listeners perceived, not the speaker's intent: the reader was given no emotion and the passages' content was meant to evoke it. The words may have driven both the reader and the listeners; the authors' content-influence flag is not in the release (2026-10-24).

KuralHub (an Interspeech 2026 survey of SER datasets) lists access as Request. Access was not checked in a primary source. Made a candidate on 2026-10-14 under the revised policy (maintainer's decision: manual access steps, label types and automatic labels are not reasons to exclude).

Second look 2026-10-28: EM2LDL (arXiv 2511.20106): 3,998 utterances (14,540 s, 4.04 h) in English, Mandarin and Cantonese with code-switching, spontaneous expressions from online platforms annotated with label distributions over 32 emotion categories (mixed emotion). Access: sign the user license agreement and return it to the author.

Emilia and YODAS audio with scores for 40 emotions + 14 attributes and emotion captions assigned automatically by EmoNet models. laion/Emolia replaced the earlier 5-way split repositories. Made a candidate on 2026-10-14 under the revised policy (maintainer's decision: manual access steps, label types and automatic labels are not reasons to exclude).

Synthetic speech from three zero-shot TTS systems (F5-TTS, CosyVoice2, StyleTTS2) imitating ESD English speakers; sentences are built so the emotion in the words usually differs from the emotion in the voice. The label is the voice emotion requested of the TTS, not a perceived emotion (a 40-listener check on a subset found 39.4-62.0% identification). Materials carry research-only and non-commercial conditions (see license_note). Whether to use synthetic data in experiments is not decided here (2026-10-24).

Implemented with 8 classes (angry / disgust / excited / happy / neutral / sad / sarcastic / surprise); uses the 1,181 clips that have audio. 24 more rows of metadata.csv (status Needs Updating) have no audio in the release and are not used; the maintainer decided not to ask the author (2026-10-26). Single speaker.

Second look 2026-10-28: test set of 1,400 utterances (7 emotions x 100 x zh/en) drawn from Emilia (in-the-wild web speech); automatic labelling followed by checking by at least two experts. CC BY-NC 4.0 (card). A test set only.
Only the bibliography of the paper (SPECOM 2015) was checked; abstract, full text and access were not.

Implemented with 7 classes (angry / boredom / disgust / fear / happy / neutral / sad); uses all 816 clips of EmoDB 2.0 (the 281 ambiguous clips can be switched by a setting and are included in train and valid by default). The license is taken from the EmoDB 2.0 record on Zenodo (CC BY 4.0) although the release's own db.yaml says CC0-1.0.

First review 2026-10-28: the Hugging Face repository is restricted (owner approval) and its page could not be read, so labels, size and license were not verified. DB values (400 h, Mandarin, acted) remain unverified.

Second look 2026-10-28: 1,115 clips (mean 3.5 s, 48 kHz mono) cut from 43 films, original English and dubbed Italian / Spanish, with anger, contempt, happiness, fear and sadness; the Interspeech 2018 paper compares categorical and dimensional perception. Restricted on Zenodo: send an EULA signed by a permanent university staff member from an institutional e-mail.

Implemented with 30 classes (vocal bursts); uses all 32,130 clips including 20 byte-identical pairs. Labels are the category the speaker meant to express; no listener rated them. Quality control was done by one person (the paper's author), who judged from a North American English perspective.

KuralHub (an Interspeech 2026 survey of SER datasets) lists access as Request. Access was not checked in a primary source. Made a candidate on 2026-10-14 under the revised policy (maintainer's decision: manual access steps, label types and automatic labels are not reasons to exclude).

Second look 2026-10-28: Spanish elicited-emotion database: 50 subjects, 12 sentences, six Ekman emotions plus a neutral tone, 3,550 audios in the feature set, validated by a crowdsourcing perception test that removed noisy samples (paper abstract on figshare). The figshare deposit has only features (a 1.2 GB COMPARE feature zip) and an agreement document; the audio is obtained through the agreement.

The audio is synthetic (GPT-4 OmniAudio, 11 voices, 4 languages). The 12,600 Bench items were rated by 2-4 of 6 psychology experts; about 4.7k were unanimous (abstract). Made a candidate on 2026-10-14 under the revised policy (maintainer's decision: manual access steps, label types and automatic labels are not reasons to exclude).

Released for research. Submit the Google Form (EULA) in the GitHub README from an institutional e-mail; login details arrive in about a week. Not given to personal accounts. Made a candidate on 2026-10-14 under the revised policy (maintainer's decision: manual access steps, label types and automatic labels are not reasons to exclude).
Only emotion captions (JSON) for ESD and IEMOCAP audio. No audio included.

Implemented with 4 classes (angry / calm / fear / happy); uses 6,530 of the 7,735 clips. The 1,116 `background` clips are left out: they hold only environmental sound, no speech (the maintainer listened, 2026-10-24), although they carry emotion tags. The one clip with emotion None and 88 duplicates are also left out. Keywords are not spread evenly over emotions (see lexical_confound_note).

First review 2026-10-28: the 30,526-sentence in-house EMOSpeech corpus (41.6 h, 5 female and 2 male speakers, Mandarin; 3-5 human emotion captions and emotion labels per clip) is not released; only the 600-sentence test set is public.
Made a candidate on 2026-10-14 under the revised policy (maintainer's decision: manual access steps, label types and automatic labels are not reasons to exclude).

Second look 2026-10-28: EmoTa: 936 utterances, 22 Sri Lankan Tamil actors, 19 neutral sentences x 5 emotions (anger, happiness, sadness, fear, neutral), Fleiss kappa 0.74 (CHiPSAL 2025 paper). Hugging Face click-through (gated: auto), CC BY-NC 4.0 per the DB. Small.

Implemented with 5 classes (angry / boredom / happy / neutral / sad); uses all 800 clips. No license text: the datasheet says copyright, no license, and asks to cite the paper, which is treated as the terms of use (maintainer's decision, 2026-10-26; asking the authors is optional). The recipe trains on the enacted emotion; the three annotators' perceived labels exist in annotations.csv and are not used.

Second look 2026-10-28: '€motion' database: emotional sentences elicited in four languages (Italian, French, English, German), used for global/local prosodic feature classification (Speech Prosody 2010 abstract); distribution and license not found.
Implemented with 5 classes (neutral / angry / happy / sad / fear). Labels are the listeners' final labels (`best_emo`). Uses 953 clips.

All 19,250 utterances are used (23.60 h); nothing is filtered. The recipe uses the audio-only labels (annotators heard the audio alone). A second set of labels from audio plus video is also distributed and is not used.

First review 2026-10-28: Korean multi-emotion TTS corpus (KAIST / Selvas AI) distributed under CC BY-NC-SA, research use only; only a small part (about 300 files of 6,000) is on GitHub and the full set needs an application and review.

Described as synthetic speech whose emotion changes 1-3 times. The paper says it will be released, but no distribution location could be confirmed. Added at the request of the literature database (2026-10-23).
Implemented with 4 classes (angry / happy / neutral / sad). Uses all 377 clips.
emoUERJ (Zenodo 5427549) reorganised for Speech Emotion Diarization (card). The original emoUERJ is a separate row (candidate).

Implemented with 5 classes (amused / angry / disgust / neutral / sleepy); uses all 6,893 files that exist (the listing says 7,000). josh recorded only 3 emotions, so for him the speaker partly determines the label. No listening test was found.

Labels are sentiment polarity (-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1), not emotion categories. Made a candidate on 2026-10-14 under the revised policy (maintainer's decision: manual access steps, label types and automatic labels are not reasons to exclude).

Implemented with 7 classes; uses all 588 clips. No license is stated in the zip or the paper and the official page is down, so the license needs confirmation (on hold, low priority: small, and other Italian datasets exist; see the needs-confirmation list). A listening test (80% overall) exists.

All audio is synthesised with OpenAI's GPT-4o-audio (texts and emotion descriptions with GPT-4o). The training data of that model is not public, and OpenAI's service terms may reach its output, so use needs to be considered in addition to the fact that the speech is synthetic (maintainer, 2026-10-24). Whether to use it is not decided here. Implemented with 7 classes; uses the 22,100 clips named in the official lists, not the 2,823 extra wav files.

Second look 2026-10-28: 999 spontaneous Spanish voice messages (messaging app) from 100 speakers; expert categories (7: happiness 342, disgust 8, anger 199, surprise 118, fear 35, sadness 72, neutral 225) plus valence/arousal from three non-experts and two experts. Public Zenodo files (labels, transcripts, features) are CC BY 4.0, but the raw audio needs an agreement signed by the institution's representative and sent to the authors; effectively research-only.

Implemented with 7 classes (angry / disgust / fear / happy / neutral / sad / surprise); uses all 6,902 clips with the official speaker-independent split. Labels are the actors' intention; five listener evaluations per clip are distributed and not used (single answers match the intention 66.4%).

Implemented with 6 classes (angry / disgust / fear / happy / sad / surprise); uses 1,287 of the 1,293 AVI files (43 subjects). Subject 6 (6 files, one long unsegmented session per emotion of 56-107 s with instructions and retakes) is left out; subject 23 lacks 3 recordings and its other 27 are used. The five sentences of each emotion differ from those of the other emotions, so the words reveal the label completely.

Labels are three dimensions, valence, arousal, dominance (1-5); no categorical emotions. Readme.txt in the zip says "Labeled with emotional dimensions: Valence, arousal and dominance (1 to 5)", and file names are numeric codes only, such as Audio1_1-02-03-03.wav (zip read via HTTP Range, 2026-10-14). Released on Zenodo under CC BY 4.0 (the description says research use only). 3,764 wav files, 15 more than the 3,749 utterances reported. Made a candidate on 2026-10-14 under the revised policy (maintainer's decision: manual access steps, label types and automatic labels are not reasons to exclude).

Implemented with 5 classes (angry / happy / neutral / sad / surprise), 35,000 clips used (29.07 h). Research use only: the license form has to be sent to the authors before use (maintainer's decision, 2026-10-26). No listening test of the labels was found.
Implemented with the 6 classes of version 1.2. Uses 2,976 clips after removing 12 near-duplicate pairs (24 clips, the same sound under different labels).
